title: Behind the Volume Knob Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav turns the volume knob on a speaker and the music grows louder smoothly, with no steps. What is behind that knob? In this animated lesson we meet the resistor (a part that opposes current, measured in ohms), watch the current fall on a live circuit as the resistance goes up, and split resistors into two families: fixed and variable. Then the fixed kinds (carbon composition, carbon film, metal film and wire wound) and the variable kinds (potentiometer, rheostat and preset).

On a live breadboard we build a volume control: a potentiometer with the music signal across its ends, and the oscilloscope showing the full input on channel one and the speaker's share on channel two, growing and shrinking as the wiper slides. We derive the voltage divider step by step (Rx = (x/L) R, Vout = Vin Rx/R), work out a full example (2.7 V from a 10 kilo ohm pot on 9 V), and finish with the exam trap (potentiometer vs rheostat), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question on a loaded divider with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 25 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
